newsitem.title: USA: American Industrial to fight court judgement.
newsitem.headline: American Industrial to fight court judgement.

text.p: American Industrial Properties REIT said on Tuesday it would seek reconsideration after a federal court ruled a company bylaw prohibiting more than 9.8 percent ownership of its outstanding shares was invalid.
The U.S. District Court in Dallas said last week the bylaw, a so-called excess share provision, was invalid under the Texas REIT act, the company said.

"We are disappointed with the court's ruling in view of the fact that the Trust's (American Industrial) Excess Share Provision is consistent with similar provisions used by other REITS and is necessary to protect the Trust's qualification as a REIT for federal income tax purposes," American Industrial President Charles Wolcott said.
Pure World Inc and its chairman had filed a motion for a partial summary judgement against American Industrial over a lawsuit associated with the bylaw.

American Industrial filed a lawsuit against Pure World and its chairman in January after Pure World won a plurality of votes cast at the December 1995 American Industrial annual meeting, Pure World said.
